rationale: SCD1 swift twin (#939, full extent on 554 files of swift-nio): the pinned grammar wraps a force unwrap in a `postfix_expression` (assignment > directly_assignable_expression > navigation_expression > postfix_expression > navigation_expression ...). The gate's climb listed only directly_assignable_expression / navigation_expression / navigation_suffix, so the inner navigation hit a wall at `postfix_expression`, the LHS-span test never ran, and a WRITE was published as a read: `uses -> value` for `box.value!.total = 0` (FileInfoTests.swift, 21 identical sibling lines, all real-corpus only — the 60-file canonical draw never contained the shape). The gate now climbs through the wrapper, so every segment of an assignment LHS is a write (outer `total` and inner `value`). The positive half pins that the same wrapper in VALUE position is still a genuine read: readThroughUnwrap/readOuterThroughUnwrap emit their member reads, so the fix cannot be widened into suppression of the wrapper. FLAT-ROW addendum: #939's table has two rows, and the fixture pinned only the nested one. `writeFlatThroughUnwrap` pins `box.value! = Inner()` — the wrapper AS the whole assignable path, the row BOTH sides used to publish as a read. It is appended at the end of the class so the existing read pins keep their lines.
